items.title: Kac chaos with explicit k/sqrt(N) and k/N total-variation rates for the canonical tensor product
items.author: Pietro Caputo; Daniel Parisi
items.work: Nonlinear recombinations and generalized random transpositions
items.difficulty_reason: The claim carries two different total-variation rates for the same object - Ck/sqrt(N) for an arbitrary admissible sequence and Ck/N for the canonical sequence rho^pi_N - so the proof cannot stop at an asymptotic local CLT. It inverts the Fourier transform of the measure conditioned on Omega_{rho_N} and works with the quotient (eq:chao5) of two such integrals, using the exponential bound |psi_N(s)| <= exp(-a<s,s>/N) from the irreducibility lemma to dominate the denominator and the far region (source 626-642), and then needs the exact second moment k^2<V_1^{-1/2}s, pi-rho_N>^2 + k<s,s> together with the assumption <pi-rho_N, pi-rho_N> = O(1/N) to reach Ck/sqrt(N) (643-656). The sharper k/N display is not a rescaling of the first: it subtracts the linear approximation g = (1/k)<V_1^{-1}v, S_k> so that the first-order term vanishes identically (662-668), uses the O(1/N^2) accuracy of the canonical sequence twice (line 658 and (eq:chaoap1)), and still has to prove a fourth-moment bound of order k^2 (702-716).

primary.label: Theorem th:eqens: total-variation rate Ck/sqrt(N) for any admissible sequence and Ck/N for the canonical sequence

proof_spans.label: complete author proof: conditioned-measure Fourier quotient, exponential characteristic-function bound, covariance estimate, and the linear-approximation subtraction giving the k/N rate
